engine.notes: Chicago remains the deepest scene: Second City, iO and the Annoyance each run a full ladder and nightly shows, and a ring of neighborhood theaters (CIC, Logan Square Improv, the Revival, the new Home) adds free or $5 stages. ComedySportz Chicago's site was unreachable at checking time, so it is unlisted; Oak Park and Evanston have classes but no dedicated improv theater.

entries.name: The Second City
entries.summary: The original sketch-and-improv institution at 230 W North Avenue since 1959, with Mainstage and e.t.c. revues, Judy's Beat Lounge, and a training center teaching Improv 1-5, the Conservatory and musical improv.
entries.schedule: Shows nightly; fall 2026 classes run late October to December; free community jams
signals: Free BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ community jams
Mainstage, e.t.c. and Judy's Beat Lounge
entries.reasons: Unmatched history and alumni, a permanent complex, a complete curriculum with fall 2026 terms posted and free jams.

entries.name: iO Theater
entries.summary: The home of the Harold since 1981, at 1501 N Kingsbury Street since 2014, with improv, sketch and stand-up six nights a week, a five-level training center and free weekly jams.
entries.schedule: Shows six nights a week; free Early Bird jam Saturdays 3:30pm; Green Room jam Wednesdays
signals: Free Saturday jam open to all students
Student ID gives free show entry
Alumni include Poehler, Hader and Farley
entries.reasons: Forty-five years, a large venue of its own, a five-level ladder, nightly shows and free jams; the classes page still showed an April 2026 session when read.

entries.name: The Annoyance Theatre & Bar
entries.summary: Mick Napier's irreverent theater at 851 W Belmont Avenue, more than 35 years old, with shows seven nights a week and the Annoyance Philosophy classes AP1-AP5 running from beginner to an ensemble show.
entries.schedule: Shows seven nights; classes Mon-Thu 6:30pm and weekends 1pm; free Music Jam Tuesdays 6:30pm
entries.reasons: A long history, its own stage and bar, a five-level curriculum and a weekly free jam; term start dates are not listed on the training page.

entries.name: CIC Theater
entries.summary: A community improv theater at 4301 N Western Avenue with free shows Tuesday to Friday, an open-stage night where anyone can play, and a five-level program from CIC Fundamentals to Performance.
entries.schedule: Free shows Tue-Fri; Open Stage Thursdays 7pm; Levels 1-5 start October 12-18, 2026
signals: Free shows four nights a week
entries.reasons: Its own room, free weekly shows, an open stage and a five-level ladder with October 2026 dates; a smaller profile than the big three.

entries.name: Logan Square Improv
entries.summary: A 501(c)(3) BYOB improv theater at 2825 W Diversey Avenue with $5 shows Wednesday to Sunday and a three-level, eight-week class program whose students perform on the weekly Thursday show.
entries.reasons: A venue of its own, shows five nights a week and a ladder with current dates; three levels and a short history keep it below the majors.

entries.name: Baby Wants Candy
entries.area: Old Town (at Judy's Beat Lounge, Second City)
entries.summary: The completely improvised full-band musical, playing Saturdays at 8:30pm in Judy's Beat Lounge at The Second City, with tickets listed through October 2026 and workshops offered by the ensemble.
entries.schedule: Saturdays 8:30pm; dates listed October 3, 10, 17 and beyond
signals: Chicago, New York, LA and touring companies
entries.reasons: A long-running weekly musical-improv show with current dates at a major venue; it is a show rather than a training path.

entries.name: Improvised Shakespeare Company
entries.summary: The company that improvises a full Elizabethan-style play from one title suggestion, resident at iO since 2006 with shows every Friday and Saturday at 7:30pm.
entries.schedule: Fridays and Saturdays 7:30pm at 1501 N Kingsbury
entries.reasons: A twenty-year weekly residency at a major theater; it is a show, not a school, and the site posts the weekly slot rather than dates.

entries.name: The Revival
entries.summary: The South Side's improv theater, founded in 2015 in homage to the Compass Players, with an adult program of five eight-week courses from Improv 101 Foundations to a 501 performance on The Revival stage.
entries.schedule: Improv 101-501 in eight-week terms; registration via ThunderTix
signals: Only improv theater on the South Side
entries.reasons: Ten years, a clear five-course ladder and press, but the site shows no show calendar, address or term dates.

entries.name: The Home Comedy Theater
entries.summary: A new 80-seat improv theater with bar and kitchen at 2843 N Halsted Street, founded 2024, already enrolling a five-level improv program with Levels 1 and 3 starting in October 2026 ahead of its official opening.
entries.schedule: Level 1 starts October 19 and 25, Level 3 October 24, 2026
entries.reasons: Current class dates and a purpose-built room, but the theater is still pre-opening, so shows and standing are unproven.

entries.name: Piven Theatre Workshop
entries.summary: The Evanston theater school founded by Byrne and Joyce Piven more than fifty years ago, built on improvisation and theater games, offering adult classes alongside its youth program at 927 Noyes Street.
entries.schedule: Adult fall classes start October 21 and 23, 2026
signals: Alumni include John and Joan Cusack
entries.reasons: A half-century institution with its own home and current adult dates, though it teaches theater through improvisation rather than running improv comedy shows.

entries.name: The Playground Theater
entries.summary: Chicago's ensemble-run improv theater, founded 1997, which left Halsted Street in the pandemic, produced shows around the city and reopened in 2025 at 4416 N Clark Street above MyBuddy's.
entries.schedule: Shows upstairs at 4416 N Clark and online; see the site calendar
entries.reasons: A long history and a new permanent home, but a sparse site with no visible schedule or classes when read.

entries.name: Comedy Plex
entries.summary: Oak Park's comedy theater and training center at 1128 Lake Street (lower level), with an eight-week adult improv class on Tuesday nights ending in a graduation show, Thursday Night Out and an open mic.
entries.schedule: Adult improv Tuesdays 7-9pm in eight-week terms; last listed term January-February 2026
signals: Graduation show on the Comedy Plex stage
Thursday Night Out and open mic
Hosts the Funny Is Female festival
entries.reasons: A permanent suburban venue with a real class, but the only term on the site had already closed and the show pages did not render.

entries.name: Oak Park Improv
entries.summary: A volunteer community group spreading improv in Oak Park: an eight-week adult fundamentals class through the Park District and free Open Stage nights at the main library where teams and walk-ins play long form.
entries.schedule: Adult class Wednesdays 7pm, September 23-November 11, 2026; Open Stage at the library
signals: Classes via the Park District of Oak Park
Free Open Stage at Oak Park Library
entries.reasons: Current dates and a free open stage, but a volunteer group with borrowed rooms, one class level and no ticketed shows.

entries.name: The Comedy Clubhouse
entries.summary: A comedy venue at 1462 N Ashland Avenue, open since 2015, mixing improv, stand-up and scripted comedy, with improv from its One Group Mind performers and workshops for schools and businesses.
entries.reasons: A real room with ten years behind it, but improv shares the bill and there is no public class program or visible calendar.
